speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine, thank you for being here tonight, and, Governor Pence, welcome. It is so great to be back at Longwood University in Farmville, Virginia.

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor Pence?

speaker: Pence
text: Well, first off, thank you, Elaine, and thank you to — thank you to Norwood University for their wonderful hospitality and the Commission on Presidential Debates. It’s deeply humbling for me to be here, to be surrounded by my — my wonderful family.

speaker: Quijano
text: Senator Kaine, on the campaign trail, you praised Secretary Clinton’s character, including her commitment to public service, yet 60 percent of voters don’t think she’s trustworthy. Why do so many people distrust her? Is it because they have questions about her e-mails and the Clinton Foundation?

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine, let me tell you why I trust Hillary Clinton. Here’s what people should look at as they look at a public servant. Do they have a passion in their life that showed up before they were in public life? And have they held onto that passion throughout their life, regardless of whether they were in office or not, succeeding or failing?

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor Pence, let me ask you, you have said Donald Trump is, quote, “thoughtful, compassionate, and steady.” Yet 67 percent of voters feel he is a risky choice, and 65 percent feel he does not have the right kind of temperament to be president. Why do so many Americans think Mr. Trump is simply too erratic?

speaker: Pence
text: Well, let me — let me say first and foremost that, Senator, you and Hillary Clinton would know a lot about an insult-driven campaign. It really is remarkable. At a time when literally, in the wake of Hillary Clinton’s tenure as secretary of state, where she was the architect of the Obama administration’s foreign policy, we see entire portions of the world, particularly the wider Middle East, literally spinning out of control. I mean, the situation we’re watching hour by hour in Syria today is the result of the failed foreign policy and the weak foreign policy that Hillary Clinton helped lead in this administration and create. The newly emboldened — the aggression of Russia, whether it was in Ukraine or now their heavy-handed approach…

speaker: Kaine
text: You guys love Russia. You both have said…

speaker: Pence
text: … their heavy-handed approach.

speaker: Kaine
text: You both have said — you both have said Vladimir Putin is a better leader than the president.

speaker: Pence
text: Well…[crosstalk]

speaker: Quijano
text: Well, we’re going to get to Russia in just a moment. But I do want to get back to the question at…

speaker: Pence
text: But in the midst — Elaine, thank you. Thank you. Thank you, Senator, I’ll…

speaker: Kaine
text: These guys have praised Vladimir Putin as a great leader. How can that…[crosstalk]

speaker: Quijano
text: Yes, and we will get to that, Senator. We do have that coming up here. But in the meantime, the questions…

speaker: Pence
text: Well, Senator, I must have hit a…[crosstalk]…I must have hit a nerve here.

speaker: Quijano
text: Why the disconnect?

speaker: Pence
text: Because at a time of great challenge in the life of this nation, where we’ve weakened America’s place in the world, stifled America’s economy, the campaign of Hillary Clinton and Tim Kaine has been an avalanche of insults.

speaker: Kaine
text: And paid few taxes and lost a billion a year.

speaker: Quijano
text: And why the disconnect with your running mate?

speaker: Pence
text: But there’s a — there’s a reason why people question the trustworthiness of Hillary Clinton. And that’s because they’re paying attention. I mean, the reality is, when she was secretary of state, Senator, come on. She had a Clinton Foundation accepting contributions from foreign governments.

speaker: Kaine
text: You are Donald Trump’s apprentice. Let me talk about this…[crosstalk]

speaker: Pence
text: Senator, I think I’m still on my time.

speaker: Kaine
text: Well, I think — isn’t this a discussion?

speaker: Quijano
text: This is our open discussion.

speaker: Kaine
text: Yeah, let’s talk about the state of…[crosstalk]

speaker: Pence
text: Well, let me interrupt — let me interrupt you and finish my sentence, if I can.

speaker: Kaine
text: Finish your sentence.

speaker: Pence
text: The Clinton Foundation accepted foreign contributions from foreign governments and foreign donors while she was secretary of state.

speaker: Kaine
text: OK, now I can weigh in. Now…

speaker: Pence
text: She had a private server…

speaker: Kaine
text: Now, I get to weigh in. Now, let me just say this…

speaker: Pence
text: … that was discovered…[crosstalk]

speaker: Quijano
text: … Senator, you have an opportunity to respond.

speaker: Pence
text: … keep that pay to play process out of the reach of the public.

speaker: Kaine
text: Governor Pence — Governor Pence doesn’t think the world’s going so well and he, you know, is going to say it’s everybody’s fault.

speaker: Kaine
text: Let me tell you this. When Hillary Clinton became secretary of state, Governor Pence, do you know that Osama bin Laden was alive?

speaker: Kaine
text: Do you know that we had 175,000 troops deployed in the battlefield in Iraq and Afghanistan? Do you know that Iran was racing toward a nuclear weapon and Russia was expanding its stockpile?

speaker: Pence
text: Eliminate the Iranian nuclear weapons program?

speaker: Kaine
text: Absolutely, without firing a shot. And instead of 175,000 American troops deployed overseas, we now have 15,000.

speaker: Pence
text: Right and…

speaker: Kaine
text: These are very, very good things.

speaker: Pence
text: And Iraq has been overrun by ISIS, because Hillary Clinton failed to renegotiate…

speaker: Kaine
text: Well, if you want to put more American troops in Iraq, you can propose that.

speaker: Pence
text: Hillary Clinton — Hillary Clinton — Hillary Clinton failed to renegotiate a status of forces agreement…

speaker: Kaine
text: No, that is incorrect. That’s incorrect.

speaker: Pence
text: And so we removed — we removed all of our…

speaker: Quijano
text: Gentlemen, we’ll get to…[crosstalk]

speaker: Pence
text: … troops from Iraq, and ISIS was able to be conjured up in that vacuum.

speaker: Kaine
text: But I’d like to correct…

speaker: Pence
text: … and overrun vast areas of Iraq.

speaker: Kaine
text: Governor, President Bush said we would leave Iraq at the end of 2011. And, Elaine, Iraq didn’t want our troops to stay, and they wouldn’t give us the protection for our troops. And guess what? If a nation where our troops are serving does not want us to stay, we’re not going to stay without their protection.

speaker: Pence
text: It was a failure of the secretary of state…

speaker: Quijano
text: We need to move on to the next topic, gentlemen.

speaker: Kaine
text: If Governor Pence wants to put more troops back in Iraq, that’s…

speaker: Quijano
text: There are a lot of people wondering in this country about the economy. Let’s turn to the issue of the economy.

speaker: Quijano
text: According to the nonpartisan Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget, neither of your economic plans will reduce the growing $19 trillion gross national debt. In fact, your plans would add even more to it.

speaker: Pence
text: I think the fact that — that under this past administration of which Hillary Clinton was a part, we’ve almost doubled the national debt is atrocious. I mean, I’m very proud of the fact that — I come from a state that works. The state of Indiana has balanced budgets. We cut taxes, we’ve made record investments in education and in infrastructure, and I still finish my term with $2 billion in the bank.

speaker: Quijano
text: Senator Kaine?

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine, on the economy, there’s a fundamental choice for the American electorate. Do you want a “you’re hired” president in Hillary Clinton or do you want a “you’re fired” president in Donald Trump? I think that’s not such a hard choice.

speaker: Quijano
text: On that point, Governor Pence, recently the New York Times released part of Mr. Trump’s 1995 tax return and reported that he could have avoided paying federal income taxes for years. Yesterday, Mr. Trump said he brilliantly used the laws to pay as little tax as legally possible. Does that seem fair to you?

speaker: Pence
text: Well, first, let me say, I appreciated the “you’re hired,” “you’re fired” thing, Senator. You use that a whole lot. And I think your running mate used a lot of pre-done lines.

speaker: Kaine
text: Fifteen million new jobs?

speaker: Pence
text: … slowest economic recovery since the Great Depression.

speaker: Kaine
text: Fifteen million new jobs?

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor…[crosstalk]

speaker: Pence
text: There are millions more people living in poverty today than the day that Barack Obama with Hillary Clinton at his side…

speaker: Kaine
text: And the poverty level and the median income…

speaker: Pence
text: … stepped into the Oval Office.

speaker: Kaine
text: … improved dramatically between 2014 and 2015.

speaker: Pence
text: You — honestly, Senator, you can roll out the numbers and the sunny side, but I got to tell you, people in Scranton know different. People in Fort Wayne, Indiana, know different. I mean, this economy is struggling. The answer to this economy is not more taxes.

speaker: Kaine
text: But it’s not the giveaway tax relief to the folks at the top.

speaker: Pence
text: It’s not more spending…[crosstalk]

speaker: Kaine
text: I am interested to hear whether he’ll defend his running mate’s not releasing taxes and not paying taxes.

speaker: Pence
text: Absolutely I will.

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor, with all due respect, the question was about whether it seems fair to you that Mr. Trump said he brilliantly used the laws to pay as little tax as legally possible.

speaker: Pence
text: Well, this is probably the difference between Donald Trump and Hillary Clinton and Senator Kaine. And, I mean, Hillary Clinton and Senator Kaine — God bless you for it, career public servants, that’s great — Donald Trump is a businessman, not a career politician. He actually built a business.

speaker: Kaine
text: But why won’t he release his tax returns?

speaker: Pence
text: Well, we’re answering the question about — about a business thing, is he…

speaker: Kaine
text: I do want to come back to that, but…

speaker: Pence
text: His tax returns — his tax returns showed he went through a very difficult time, but he used the tax code just the way it’s supposed to be used. And he did it brilliantly.

speaker: Kaine
text: How do you know that? You haven’t seen his tax returns.

speaker: Pence
text: He created a runway — because he’s created a business that’s worth billions of dollars today.

speaker: Kaine
text: How do you know that?

speaker: Pence
text: And with regard to paying taxes, this whole riff about not paying taxes and people saying he didn’t pay taxes for years, Donald Trump has created tens of thousands of jobs. And he’s paid payroll taxes, sales taxes, property taxes…

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine, let me talk about something.

speaker: Quijano
text: Senator, I’m going to give you about 30 seconds to respond, and I have question on Social Security for you.

speaker: Pence
text: The only issue on taxes — Hillary Clinton is going to raise taxes, and Donald Trump and I are going to cut them.

speaker: Kaine
text: Donald Trump started this campaign in 2014 and he said, “If I run for president, I will absolutely release my taxes.” He’s broken his first…

speaker: Pence
text: And he will.

speaker: Kaine
text: He’s broken his first promise. Second, he stood on the stage…

speaker: Pence
text: He hasn’t broken his promise. He said he’s…

speaker: Kaine
text: He stood on the stage last week and when Hillary said, you haven’t been paying taxes, he said, “That makes me smart.” So it’s smart not to pay for our military? It’s smart not to pay for veterans? It’s smart not to pay for teachers? And I guess all of us who do pay for those things, I guess we’re stupid. And the last thing I’ll say is this…

speaker: Pence
text: Senator, do you take all the deductions that you’re entitled to?

speaker: Kaine
text: The last thing — the last thing I want to ask Governor Pence is…

speaker: Kaine
text: Governor Pence had to give Donald Trump his tax returns to show he was qualified to be vice president. Donald Trump must give the American public his tax returns to show that he’s qualified to be president. And he’s breaking his promise.

speaker: Pence
text: Elaine, I have to respond to this.

speaker: Quijano
text: You get very little time, 20 seconds.

speaker: Pence
text: I’ll be — I’ll be very respectful.

speaker: Pence
text: Look, Donald Trump has filed over 100 pages of financial disclosure, which is what the law requires.

speaker: Kaine
text: But he said he would release his tax returns.

speaker: Quijano
text: All right, Gentlemen…

speaker: Pence
text: The American people can review that. And he’s going — Senator, he’s going to release his tax returns when the audit is over…

speaker: Quijano
text: … I need to ask you about Social Security…

speaker: Kaine
text: Richard Nixon released tax returns when he was under audit.

speaker: Pence
text: They’re going to raise your taxes. We’re going to cut your taxes.

speaker: Quijano
text: Gentlemen…

speaker: Kaine
text: If you can’t meet Nixon’s standard…

speaker: Quijano
text: The people at home cannot understand either one of you when you speak over each other. I would please ask you to wait until it is that the other is finished.

speaker: Kaine
text: All right. We’re having fun up here.

speaker: Quijano
text: Senator Kaine, on the issue of Social Security, in 18 years, when the Social Security Trust Funds run out of money, you’ll be 76. The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget estimates your benefits could be cut by as much as $7,500 per year. What would your administration do to prevent this cut?

speaker: Kaine
text: First, we’re going to protect Social Security, which is one of the greatest programs that the American government has ever done. It happened at a time when you would work your whole life, your whole life, raising your kids, working, being a Little League coach or a Sunday school teacher, and then you would retire into poverty. And Social Security has enabled people to retire with dignity and overwhelmingly not be in poverty.

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor Pence, I’ll give you an opportunity to respond.

speaker: Pence
text: Well, thanks, Elaine. There they go again. OK…

speaker: Kaine
text: Go read — go read the book.

speaker: Pence
text: All Donald Trump — all Donald Trump and I have said about Social Security is we’re going to meet our obligations to our seniors. That’s it.

speaker: Kaine
text: Go read the book.

speaker: Pence
text: We’ve said we’re going to meet the obligations of Medicare. That’s what this campaign is really about, Senator. And I get, this is — this is the old scare tactic that they roll out…

speaker: Kaine
text: But — but you have a voting record, Governor.

speaker: Pence
text: And I get all of that. I just, look…

speaker: Pence
text: There’s a question that you asked a little bit earlier that I want to go back to.

speaker: Kaine
text: I can’t believe that you won’t defend your own voting record.

speaker: Pence
text: I have to go back to.

speaker: Pence
text: Well, look, I — you’re running with Hillary Clinton, who wants to raise taxes by $1 trillion, increase spending by $2 trillion, and you say you’re going to keep the promises of Social Security. Donald Trump and I are going to cut taxes. We’re going to — we’re going to — we’re going to…

speaker: Kaine
text: You’re not going to cut taxes. You’re going to raise taxes on the middle class.

speaker: Pence
text: … reform government programs so we can meet the obligations of Social Security and Medicare.

speaker: Quijano
text: All right. PENCE: Stay on the path that your party has us on, we’re going to be in a — in a mountain range of debt. And we’re going to face hard choices and…[crosstalk]

speaker: Kaine
text: You did ask this question about debt, and the debt explosion on the Trump plan is much, much bigger than anything on the Clinton side.

speaker: Quijano
text: All right. Let me move on now…

speaker: Pence
text: Three hundred and five economists said your plan is bad for the economy.

speaker: Quijano
text: … to the issue of law enforcement and race relations. Law enforcement and race relations. After the Dallas police shooting, Police Chief David Brown said, quote, “We’re asking cops to do too much in this country. Every societal failure we put it off on the cops to solve. Not enough mental health funding, not enough drug addiction funding, schools fail, let’s give it to the cops.”

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine, I think that’s a very fair comment. I think we put a lot on police shoulders. And this is something I got a lot of scar tissue and experience on.

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor Pence?

speaker: Pence
text: You know, my uncle was a cop, a career cop, on the beat in downtown Chicago. He was my hero when I was growing up. And we’d go up to visit my dad’s family in Chicago. My three brothers and I would marvel at my uncle when he would come out in his uniform, sidearm at his side.

speaker: Kaine
text: Can I — can I explain…

speaker: Pence
text: … I just think what we ought to do is we ought to stop seizing on these moments of tragedy. We ought to assure the public that we’ll have a full and complete and transparent investigation whenever there’s a loss of life because of police action. But, Senator, please, you know, enough of this seeking every opportunity to demean law enforcement broadly by making the accusation of implicit bias every time tragedy occurs.

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine — Elaine, people shouldn’t be afraid to bring up issues of bias in law enforcement. And if you’re afraid to have…

speaker: Pence
text: I’m not afraid to bring that up.

speaker: Kaine
text: And if — if you’re afraid to have the discussion, you’ll never solve it. And so here’s — here’s an example, heartbreaking. We would agree this is a heartbreaking example.

speaker: Pence
text: We need criminal justice reform.

speaker: Kaine
text: Well, we do.

speaker: Pence
text: Indiana has passed criminal justice reform.

speaker: Kaine
text: But I just want to say, those who say that we should not…

speaker: Pence
text: But that’s not what you’re talking about.

speaker: Kaine
text: … we should not be able to bring up and talk about bias in the system, we’ll never solve the problem…

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor Pence…[crosstalk]…Governor Pence…

speaker: Pence
text: Senator, when African-American police officers involved in a police action shooting involving an African-American, why would Hillary Clinton accuse that African-American police officer of implicit bias?

speaker: Kaine
text: Well, I guess I can’t believe you are defending the position that there is no bias and it’s a topic we don’t even…[crosstalk]

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor Pence, I have a question on that point.

speaker: Pence
text: I did not make that statement. I…

speaker: Quijano
text: Your fellow Republican, Governor Pence, Senator Tim Scott, who is African-American, recently spoke on the Senate floor. He said he was stopped seven times by law enforcement in one year.

speaker: Kaine
text: A U.S. senator.

speaker: Quijano
text: He said, “I have felt the anger, the frustration, the sadness, and the humiliation that comes with feeling like you’re being targeted for nothing more than being just yourself.” What would you say to Senator Scott about his experiences?

speaker: Pence
text: Well, I have the deepest respect for Senator Scott, and he’s a close friend. And what I would say is that we — we need to adopt criminal justice reform nationally. I — I signed criminal justice reform in the state of Indiana, Senator, and we’re very proud of it.

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine, can I…

speaker: Quijano
text: So what would you say to Senator Scott, Governor?

speaker: Pence
text: Law enforcement in this country is a force for good. They are the — they truly are people that put their lives on the line every single day. But I would — I would suggest to you, what we need to do is assert a stronger leadership at the national level to support law enforcement. You just heard Senator Kaine reject stop-and-frisk. Well, I would suggest to you that the families that live in our inner cities that are besieged by crime…

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine, let me — let me…

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor, the question is about Senator Scott. What would — what would you tell Senator Scott?

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine, if I could — if I could jump in. I’ve heard Senator Scott make that eloquent plea. And look, criminal justice is about respecting the law and being respected by the law. So there is a fundamental respect issue here.

speaker: Quijano
text: All right. I want to turn to our next segment now, immigration. Your running mates have both said that undocumented immigrants who have committed violent crimes should be deported. What would you tell the millions of undocumented immigrants who have not committed violent crimes? Governor Pence?

speaker: Pence
text: Donald Trump’s laid out a plan to end illegal immigration once and for all in this country. We’ve been talking it to death for 20 years. Hillary Clinton and Tim Kaine want to continue the policies of open borders, amnesty, catch and release, sanctuary cities, all the things that are driving — that are driving wages down in this country, Senator, and also too often with criminal aliens in the country, it’s bringing heartbreak.

speaker: Pence
text: It’s my time, Senator.

speaker: Quijano
text: It is, in fact, the governor’s time.

speaker: Kaine
text: I apologize. It’s your two minutes. I apologize.

speaker: Pence
text: Thanks. I forgive you. He says ours is an insult-driven campaign. Did you all just hear that? Ours is an insult-driven campaign?

speaker: Pence
text: That’s small potatoes compared to Hillary Clinton…

speaker: Quijano
text: Senator Kaine?

speaker: Pence
text: …. calling half of Donald Trump’s supporters a basket of deplorables.

speaker: Kaine
text: Hillary Clinton said something on the campaign trail, and the very next day, she said, you know what, I shouldn’t have said that.

speaker: Pence
text: She said she shouldn’t have said half.

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor, this is Senator Kaine’s two minutes, please.

speaker: Kaine
text: Yeah, that’s right, so now we’re even.

speaker: Pence
text: Yeah. [laughter]

speaker: Kaine
text: Look for Donald Trump apologizing to John McCain for saying he wasn’t a hero…

speaker: Kaine
text: … to Donald Trump apologizing for calling women slobs, pigs, dogs, disgusting.

speaker: Pence
text: She apologized for saying “half.”

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor. It is his two minutes, please.

speaker: Kaine
text: Did Donald Trump apologize for taking after somebody in a Twitter war and making fun of her weight? Did he apologize for saying African-Americans are living in Hell? Did he apologize for saying President Obama was not even a citizen of the United States? You will look in vain to see Donald Trump ever taking responsibility for anybody and apologizing.

speaker: Pence
text: That’s nonsense. That’s nonsense.

speaker: Kaine
text: I cannot believe that Governor Pence would sit here and defend his running mate’s claim that we should create a deportation force to — so that they’ll all be gone.

speaker: Pence
text: Senator, we have a deportation force. It’s called Immigrations and Customs Enforcement. And the union for Immigrations and Customs Enforcement for the first time in their history endorsed Donald Trump to be the next president of the United States of America.

speaker: Kaine
text: So you like the 16 million deportations?

speaker: Pence
text: Senator, that’s — that’s nonsense. Look, what you just heard is they have a plan for open borders, amnesty. That’s…[crosstalk]

speaker: Kaine
text: Our plan is like Ronald Reagan’s plan from 1986.

speaker: Pence
text: They call it comprehensive immigration reform — they call it comprehensive immigration reform on Capitol Hill. We all know the routine. It’s amnesty. And you heard one of the last things he mentioned was border security.

speaker: Pence
text: They always say we’re going to do this, we’re going to do that, we’ll eventually get the border…[crosstalk]

speaker: Kaine
text: … border security three years ago, and Governor Pence was against it.

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor, Mr. Trump has said…

speaker: Pence
text: Ronald Reagan said a nation without borders is not a nation. Donald Trump is committed to restoring the borders of this nation and securing our nation, enforcing our laws.

speaker: Quijano
text: So, Governor, how would these millions of undocumented immigrants leave? Would they be forcibly removed?

speaker: Pence
text: Well, I think Donald Trump laid out a series of priorities that doesn’t ends with border security. It begins with border security. And after we secure the border, not only build a wall, but beneath the ground and in the air, we do internal enforcement.

speaker: Kaine
text: I just have to correct Governor Pence….

speaker: Pence
text: … where people can come into this country.

speaker: Kaine
text: I have to…

speaker: Pence
text: That’s the order that you should do it. Border security, removing criminal aliens, upholding with law, and then — but then, Senator, I’ll work you when you go back to the Senate, I promise you, we’ll work with you to reform the immigration system.

speaker: Kaine
text: I look forward to working together in whatever capacities we serve in. But I just want to make it very, very clear that he’s trying to fuzz up what Donald Trump has said. When Donald Trump spoke in Phoenix, he looked the audience in the eye and he said, no, we’re building a wall, and we’re deporting everybody. He said, quote, “They will all be gone.” “They will all be gone.” And this is one of these ones where you can just go to the tape on it and see what Donald Trump has said. And to add…

speaker: Pence
text: He’s talking about criminal aliens.

speaker: Kaine
text: And to add to it, and to add to it, and to add to it, we are a nation of immigrants. Mike Pence and I both are descended from immigrant families. Some things, you know, maybe weren’t said so great about the Irish when they came, but we’ve done well by absorbing immigrants, and it’s made our nation stronger.

speaker: Quijano
text: Gentleman, I’d like to shift now to the threat of terrorism. Do you think the world today is a safer or more dangerous place than it was eight years ago? Has the terrorist threat increased or decreased? Senator Kaine?

speaker: Kaine
text: The terrorist threat has decreased in some ways, because bin Laden is dead. The terrorist threat has decreased in some ways because an Iranian nuclear weapons program has been stopped. The terrorist threat to United States troops has been decreased in some ways because there’s not 175,000 in a dangerous part of the world. There’s only 15,000.

speaker: Pence
text: Oh, please. Come on.

speaker: Kaine
text: … and Saddam Hussein. And last and most dangerously, Donald Trump believes — Donald Trump believes that the world will be safer if more nations have nuclear weapons. He’s said Saudi Arabia should get them, Japan should get them, Korea should get them. And when he was confronted with this, and told, wait a minute, terrorists could get those, proliferation could lead to nuclear war, here’s what Donald Trump said, and I quote: “Go ahead, folks, enjoy yourselves.”

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor Pence?

speaker: Pence
text: Did you work on that one a long time? Because that had a lot of really creative lines in it.

speaker: Kaine
text: Well, I’m going to see if you can defend any of it.

speaker: Pence
text: Well, look, I can defend — I — I — I can — I can make very clear to the American people, after traveling millions of miles as our secretary of state, after being the architect of the foreign policy of this administration, America is less safe today than it was the day that Barack Obama became president of the United States. It’s absolutely inarguable.

speaker: Kaine
text: I was in Virginia where the Pentagon’s…[crosstalk]

speaker: Pence
text: I know you were. We all lived through that day as a nation. It was heartbreaking. And I want to give this president credit for bringing Osama bin Laden to justice.

speaker: Kaine
text: Stopping a nuclear weapons program without firing a shot?

speaker: Pence
text: You didn’t stop the nuclear weapons program.

speaker: Kaine
text: Yes, we did.

speaker: Pence
text: You essentially…

speaker: Kaine
text: Even the Israeli military says it stopped.

speaker: Pence
text: … guaranteed that Iran will someday become a nuclear power, because there’s no limitations once the period of time of the treaty comes off.

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor Pence, Mr. Trump has proposed extreme vetting of immigrants from parts of the world that export terrorism. But that does not address many of the recent terrorist attacks in the United States, such as the Orlando nightclub massacre and the recent bombings in New York and New Jersey. Those were homegrown, committed by U.S. citizens and legal residents. What specific tools would you use to prevent those kinds of attacks?

speaker: Pence
text: Well, I think it’s — I think it’s a great question, Elaine, but it really does begin with us reforming our immigration system and putting the interests, particularly the safety and security of the American people, first.

speaker: Kaine
text: Elaine, I want to…[crosstalk]

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor, the question was about homegrown.

speaker: Pence

speaker: Kaine
text: When Donald Trump says women should be punished or Mexicans are rapists and criminals…

speaker: Pence
text: I’m telling you…

speaker: Kaine
text: … or John McCain is not a hero, he is showing you who he is.

speaker: Pence
text: Senator, you’ve whipped out that Mexican thing again. He — look…

speaker: Kaine
text: Can you defend it?

speaker: Pence
text: There are criminal aliens in this country, Tim, who have come into this country illegally who are perpetrating violence and taking American lives.

speaker: Kaine
text: You want to — you want to use a big broad brush against Mexicans on that?

speaker: Pence
text: He also said and many of them are good people. You keep leaving that out of your quote. And if you want me to go there, I’ll go there.

speaker: Kaine
text: This is important —

speaker: Pence
text: … bring the — let’s welcome the children into our world. There are so many families around the country who can’t have children. We could improve adoption…

speaker: Kaine
text: But, Governor…

speaker: Pence
text: … so that families that can’t have children can adopt more readily those children from crisis pregnancies.

speaker: Kaine
text: Governor, why don’t you trust women to make this choice for themselves? We can encourage people to support life. Of course we can. But why don’t you trust women? Why doesn’t Donald Trump trust women to make this choice for themselves?

speaker: Pence
text: Because there are…

speaker: Kaine
text: … but on fundamental issues of morality, we should let women make their own decisions.

speaker: Pence
text: Because there is — a society can be judged by how it deals with its most vulnerable, the aged, the infirm, the disabled, and the unborn. I believe it with all my heart. And I couldn’t be more proud to be standing with a pro-life candidate in Donald Trump.

speaker: Quijano
text: I do have one final question for you both tonight. It has been a divisive campaign. Senator Kaine, if your ticket wins, what specifically are you going to do to unify the country and reassure the people who voted against you?

speaker: Kaine
text: That’s a really important one. That may be the $64,000 question, because it has been a divisive campaign. And again, Hillary is running a campaign about stronger together, and Donald Trump — and this is — this is not directed at this man, except to the extent that he can’t defend Donald Trump — Donald Trump has run a campaign that’s been about one insult after the next.

speaker: Quijano
text: Governor, how will you unify the country if you win?

speaker: Pence
text: Well, thank you, Elaine, and thanks for a great discussion…

speaker: Kaine
text: Absolutely.

speaker: Pence
text: … tonight. Thank you, Senator.

speaker: Quijano
text: All right, gentlemen, thank you so much.
